title: Scammers use AI-generated images of missing pets to extort owners
content_md: When your pet goes missing, it can be totally heartbreaking. So hearing that they’ve been found is no doubt very welcome news. Even better to see a photo of them looking safe and well. But while the photo may look exactly like your pet, that doesn’t mean the person who sent it has your pet or even ever saw it. The BBC reports how criminals are sending owners AI-generated images of their missing pets, demanding money for their return, and sometimes threatening to harm the animals when owners refuse to pay. The BBC interviewed two targets of this scam who were both contacted after posting a missing pet message on social media. The scammers sent them pictures of their beloved pets and demanded a ransom for their safe return. Messages like these exploit two powerful emotions in quick succession: relief that a beloved pet has been found, followed by fear that something terrible will happen unless the owner acts immediately. The scam typically follows this pattern: A scammer finds a missing pet appeal, which is typically posted to social media or local sites with an accompanying photo and contact details. The scammer contacts the owner and claims to have found the animal. An image fabricated with the help of AI makes the claim appear more convincing. They ask for money which may be described as a reward or as payment for emergency treatment . They add pressure. They might refuse to meet until payment arrives, or threaten to sell or harm the pet.
